answer.rationale: Competitive pressure on SMB pricing requires immediate response. Memory 73 shows targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory 31 confirms simplification works but is primarily an activation lever, not a retention/churn defense. Memory 57 shows referral incentives work on established customers, not acquisition or churn reversal. A standard-scale promotional pricing experiment on the SMB segment most exposed to churn addresses the immediate competitive threat while preserving the ability to layer activation messaging (memory 91) once accounts land. This avoids the risk of a broad rollout before validating price elasticity in this specific competitive context, and preserves the long-term revenue quality by treating pricing as tactical response rather than structural positioning. The downstream risk flagged: aggressive discounting may anchor price expectations and complicate future value realization, so close monitoring of qualified revenue quality and margin is essential.
